proposed.explanation: Type A alone provides no retardation; set time would be normal or fast (not extended working time). Type C (acceleration) is counter-productive in hot weather; it would shorten working time, opposite of goal. Type F provides flowing concrete but doesn't specifically address hot-weather retardation; Type D is more targeted. Type D is optimized for hot weather with competing needs: strength gain (Type A water reduction) and extended working time (Type B retardation). In 32°C tropical temperature with complex column geometry, Type D prevents premature stiffening while improving strength. Hot weather + extended workability + strength = Type D. Hot weather + rapid strength = Type C (cold weather). Always match admixture type to project conditions.
